extracted.intended_audience: patent owners, patent practitioners/attorneys, and patent examiners handling ex parte reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules governing requests for extensions of time and replies in ex parte reexamination proceedings (third-party requested, patent-owner requested, and Director-ordered), including timing, fees, required showings of cause, and limits on extensions and supplemental replies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of 37 CFR 1.136
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.136(a) and (b) are NOT applicable to ex parte reexamination proceedings under any circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions in reexamination must be requested under 37 CFR 1.550(c) because an ex parte reexamination is not an “application” and there is neither an “application” nor an “applicant” involved. Form paragraph 22.04.01 may be used to notify parties that 1.136 extensions are not permitted; reexamination extensions use 1.550(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic content and form of extension requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for an extension under 37 CFR 1.550(c) must specify the requested period of extension and be accompanied by the petition fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must be in writing, filed as a separate paper, may be filed with or without the response (but must be a separate paper), and must be filed on or before the day on which action by the patent owner is due (timing varies by type of reexamination). Certificates of mailing/transmission and Priority Mail Express procedures (37 CFR 1.8 and 1.10) may be used to file requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of consideration for extension requests
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for an extension of time in an ex parte reexamination proceeding will be considered only after the decision to grant or deny reexamination is mailed; any request filed before that decision will be denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests submitted prior to mailing of the decision to grant reexamination are not entertained. A request for extension to file a petition from denial of a request for reexamination requires a petition under 37 CFR 1.183 with the appropriate fee to waive 1.515(c) time provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee rule for extension requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(g) is required for filing a request for an extension of time in a reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike 1.136 practice for applications, the period of extension in reexamination is not determined by the amount of fee paid; the fee is only for filing the request. Timely filing of the fee alone (without required content/timing) will not effect an extension in many cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑party requested reexamination: requirement of sufficient cause
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for an extension of time for a response by the patent owner in a third party requested ex parte reexamination must include a showing of sufficient cause, and the requested extension must be for a reasonable time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No “no cause” extensions (up to two months without cause) are available in third-party requested reexaminations. The mere filing of a written request and required fee will not effect an extension. First requests will generally be granted if sufficient cause is shown (usually one month); second/subsequent requests or requests >1 month will only be granted in extraordinary situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory non-extendability of certain reply periods (37 CFR 1.535)
rubrics_metrics.description: The two-month period for filing a third party requester reply under 37 CFR 1.535 (two months from service of the patent owner’s statement) cannot be extended under any circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory periods (35 U.S.C. 304) cannot be waived or extended. See MPEP § 2251 for further discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent-owner requested or Director-ordered reexamination: no-cause extensions up to two months
rubrics_metrics.description: In patent owner requested or Director ordered ex parte reexaminations, a patent owner may request a “no cause” extension of time for up to two months from the response period set in the Office action without showing sufficient cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike 1.136 practice, the mere filing of the fee is insufficient: the patent owner must timely file (i) a written request specifying the requested period (up to two months) as a separate paper, and (ii) the fee under 1.17(g). The request and fee may be filed with or without the response, but the request, fee, and response must all be timely filed. The Office may grant the specified extension up to two months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions longer than two months: showing of sufficient cause and reasonableness
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for an extension for more than two months from the time period set in the Office action must include a showing of sufficient cause, be for a reasonable time, and will only be granted in extraordinary circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such requests must fully state reasons, include what action the patent owner has taken toward preparing a response, and provide a factual accounting of reasonably diligent behavior by all responsible for preparing the response. Timely filing of the request and fee alone will not effect an extension for >2 months. Requests are expected to be rare when patent owner already has opportunity for up to two months no-cause extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing deadlines for ‘no cause’ extensions (patent-owner/Director ordered)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for a ‘no cause’ extension of up to two months must be filed no later than two months from the expiration of the time period set in the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: if Office action sets two-month response period and patent owner requests two-month extension, file within four months from mail date; if patent owner requests one-month extension, file within three months from mail date. If Office action sets one-month period and patent owner requests two-month extension, file within three months from mail date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing deadlines for extensions > two months (patent-owner/Director ordered)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for an extension of more than two months must be filed on or before the day on which action by the patent owner is due (which depends on total prior no-cause extensions filed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If patent owner timely filed one or more no-cause requests whose total does not exceed two months, the day on which action is due is the expiration of the total of those no-cause extensions. To request >2 months, the patent owner must file (by that date) the prior no-cause request(s) and fees and an additional request for >2 months with sufficient cause and fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of extended due date when adding extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: The time extended is added to the last calendar day of the original period, not added to the due day when that last day falls on a weekend or federal holiday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This affects the calendar date used as the new last day. Any request for extension must be filed according to the specific calendar computation rules described in 37 CFR 1.550(c) and MPEP examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests must be filed as separate paper (cannot be combined with other papers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for an extension of time must be submitted as a separate paper which will be forwarded to the CRU SPRS or TC Director for action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the request and fee may be filed with or without the response, the extension request must be a separate paper from responses, appeal briefs, or other papers. Failure to file as a separate paper may result in denial or dismissal as untimely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation/examples illustrating filing windows
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific examples illustrate when a request for one- or two-month no-cause extensions or requests for >2 months must be filed given Office action response periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: (1) Office action two-month period, patent owner requests two-month extension → request and response due within four months of mail date; (2) Office action two-month period, request one-month extension → file within three months; (3) illustrations of combinations of earlier untimely filings and remedial options; see MPEP §2265 examples 1–5 for full scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of time for filing notices of appeal, appeal briefs, and reply briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions for filing a notice of appeal to the PTAB, an appeal brief, or a reply brief are governed by 37 CFR 1.550(c) and follow the same timing and cause/no-cause distinctions as responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For purposes of requesting extension the “day on which action by the patent owner is due” is the last day of the time period permitted to file the brief (e.g., appeal brief: two months from the date of the appeal). Patent owner requested or Director ordered reexaminations permit ‘no cause’ extensions up to two months for briefs if timely filed; >2 months requires sufficient cause. Requests must be separate papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balancing test for sufficient cause
rubrics_metrics.description: Any evaluation of whether sufficient cause has been shown must balance the need to provide the patent owner a fair opportunity to present argument against any attack on the patent and the statutory requirement that reexamination proceedings be conducted with special dispatch (35 U.S.C. 305).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for extension (except no-cause up to two months) must fully state the reasons and include a factual accounting of reasonably diligent behavior by those responsible. Third-party reexamination extension requests are judged more strictly; typically first requests may be granted for short periods (usually one month) if diligence shown; subsequent or longer requests only in extraordinary circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic two‑month extension for timely first response to a final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing a timely first response to a final rejection having a shortened statutory period is construed as including a request to extend the shortened statutory period an additional two months (automatic two-month extension).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This automatic extension cannot extend the period for response beyond six months from date of final action. It applies only to the first response to a final rejection and does not apply once a notice of appeal has been filed. The primary examiner may grant the implicit two-month extension and should notify patent owner of the ruling with sufficient time to act. Advisory action PTOL-467 is used to state the extension (integer months only).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on total extension for response to final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: In no case may the period for response to a final rejection be extended to exceed six months from the mailing date of the final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory actions should specify the extension in whole months (2–6). Fractions of months should not be indicated. If a second/subsequent amendment filed after extension does not place reexamination in condition for allowance, prosecution will stand terminated under 37 CFR 1.550(d) unless an appropriate notice of appeal was filed before expiration of the response period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits/declarations filed after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for extension to submit affidavits or declarations after final rejection are sometimes granted, but the granting is without prejudice to the examiner's later decision to question why the affidavit/declaration was not earlier presented; the examiner may deny entry if showing is insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Granting an extension to submit an affidavit serves merely to keep prosecution from becoming terminated while allowing the patent owner opportunity to present the affidavit. Affidavits submitted after final are subject to same treatment as amendments after final (see In re Affidavit Filed After Final Rejection). Admission or refusal to admit the affidavit will not necessarily save the prosecution from termination unless the filing places the reexamination in condition for allowance and other requirements of 37 CFR 1.113 are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental replies (37 CFR 1.111(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental reply to a reply in compliance with 37 CFR 1.111(b) will not be entered as a matter of right except in limited circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may enter a supplemental reply only if it is clearly limited to: (A) cancellation of claims; (B) adoption of the examiner's suggestions; (C) placement of the application in condition for allowance; (D) reply to an Office requirement made after the first reply was filed; (E) correction of informalities; or (F) simplification of issues for appeal. A supplemental reply will be entered if filed within the period during which action by the Office is suspended under 37 CFR 1.103(a) or (c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of advisory action when examiner cannot mail ruling timely
rubrics_metrics.description: If advisory action cannot be mailed in sufficient time for the patent owner to consider the examiner’s ruling before termination, the examiner may grant additional time to complete the response; the extension should be set forth in the advisory Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory action form PTOL-467 states: 'THE PERIOD FOR RESPONSE IS EXTENDED TO RUN ___ MONTHS FROM THE MAILING DATE OF THE FINAL REJECTION.' The number of months must be an integer (2–6). This practice ensures patent owner can consider examiner's position before being required to file notice of appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of untimely or dismissed extension requests
rubrics_metrics.description: An untimely request for extension will be dismissed even if filed within a later allowable calendar (examples provided); filing an untimely request may require refiling a different request (e.g., for two months) within the correct window to obtain any extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show dismissal of late one-month request even if within overall four-month window, and show how a subsequent timely two-month request may still be granted. The rules emphasize strict adherence to the precise filing windows described in the MPEP examples.
